<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9 \cdot \frac{1}{3} = 3</annotation></semantics></math> is the input of the logarithm; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_3 3 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Yes: both graphs pass through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which value is closest to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 6</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which value is closest to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_2 7</annotation></semantics></math>?

For <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\log_2 x - \log_2 5</annotation></semantics></math> as a single logarithm.

mistakes.why: The <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> is an exponent on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, not a factor: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\log_2 x = \log_2 x^3</annotation></semantics></math>.
A difference of logarithms is the logarithm of a quotient, not of a difference.
Subtracting logarithms divides their inputs inside one logarithm; it does not divide two logarithms.

items.q: Write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x^4) - \ln(x^2)</annotation></semantics></math> as a single logarithm that is equal to it for every <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> equals <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x^2)</annotation></semantics></math> only for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>; at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> it is undefined, while <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x^2) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
A difference of logarithms is the logarithm of a quotient, not of a difference.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^4}{x^2} = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>; and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The function <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \log_4 x</annotation></semantics></math> is a vertical dilation of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \log_2 x</annotation></semantics></math>. Write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math> as a constant times <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_2 x</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Divide by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_2 4 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_4 16 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\log_2 16 = 8</annotation></semantics></math>.

Changing the base divides the whole logarithm by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_2 4</annotation></semantics></math>; it does not divide the input by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which expression is equal to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>25</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_5(25x^3)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find the exact value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_6 4 + \log_6 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the input <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>36</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36</annotation></semantics></math>. The value is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_6 36 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use a calculator to find <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_7 20</annotation></semantics></math>, correct to three decimal places.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln \frac{20}{7}</annotation></semantics></math>. That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\ln 7}{\ln 20}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>20</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \log_{20} 7</annotation></semantics></math>, upside down.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\log x)^2 = 2\log x</annotation></semantics></math>

State where it holds: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the domain of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log x</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Solve <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_2(x + 1) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> is the change in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> per unit of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_3 x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The inputs multiply by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>, so the step of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> goes with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_3</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>≠</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\ln 3 \ne 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use the model <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 20 + 6\log_3 x</annotation></semantics></math> to predict the typing speed after <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>243</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">243</annotation></semantics></math> hours.

mistakes.why: That multiplies <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>243</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">243</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> and adds <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>. That is the speed at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>81</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81</annotation></semantics></math> hours; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>243</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">243</annotation></semantics></math> is one more factor of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>, so add <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>.
